pr.title: Print only the version when field was not built from a checkout
pr.head: af362da8e5226c0d550b78c00cb2d91412d01c72

summary: field --version tells you which build of the Field CLI is running. Its first line is the version from package.json, followed in parentheses by the Git commit the build came from, so that during development you can see whether the code you are running is the code in your checkout.

A release install is the other way to get Field: install.sh downloads GitHub's source archive of a version's tag, unpacks it into a directory of its own, and builds it there. That archive has no .git, so the build has no commit to name, and the first line read field 0.3.0  (not a git checkout). Release installs are now the usual install, so the parenthetical described the normal case as if something were missing.

This pull request makes two changes. The first prints the version alone when the build has no commit, and leaves a build from a checkout exactly as it was. The second, added after the first review, decides more strictly whether a build has a commit: the build script and the run-time read ask Git only when the package root has its own .git. Git searches upward from the directory it is asked about, so before this change a release unpacked inside another repository, such as a home directory kept in Git, reported that repository's commit as its own.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Build stamp: dist/build-info.json, which scripts/stamp-build.mjs writes at the end of pnpm build. It holds the commit, branch, and count of uncommitted files the build saw, or {} when the build has no commit.
  • Checkout: a Git clone or worktree of the repository, built in place. A clone has a .git directory at its root, and a worktree has a .git file.
  • Release install: a version's source archive, unpacked and built by install.sh, with no .git.
  • Live read: liveIdentity in version.ts, which asks Git for the checkout's commit when field --version runs, to compare with the stamp or to stand in for one.
  • Drift: the checkout moving after the build, by a new commit or by edits, which field --version reports beside the stamped commit.

groups.title: The first line of field --version
groups.kicker: The version alone when the build has no commit, and no commit borrowed from an outer repository
intro: formatVersionReport turns the version report into the text field --version prints. Its first line is field <version>, plus a parenthetical describing the build's commit when there is one: the short commit, the branch unless HEAD is detached, the count of uncommitted files at build time, and any drift since. When the report carries no commit, the parenthetical used to say not a git checkout. It is now left out.

liveIdentity, the live read, now returns no commit unless the package root has its own .git. It is the fallback when a build's stamp has no commit, so without this check a release inside another repository would have found that repository's commit at run time even with an empty stamp. It also takes the root as an optional argument, which only the tests pass.

files.note: liveIdentity checks for .git before asking Git and is exported for the tests; the formatter drops the parenthetical when there is no commit.

checks.text: install.sh and isCheckout in src/commands/upgrade.ts already tell a checkout from a release by the same .git test, so the version report now agrees with them about which installs are checkouts.

An archive of this head built under a directory that is itself a Git repository printed field 0.3.0, and so did one built outside any repository. The checkout cases printed the forms in the overview's table.

files.note: Formatter cases with and without a commit, and a new a release unpacked inside another repository block that runs the real stamp script and liveIdentity in temporary repositories.

checks.text: The review removed the .git check from liveIdentity alone, and the release case failed here; with the check removed from both places, it failed at the stamp. windows CI runs the clone and worktree case too, and passed.

groups.title: How the build stamp finds its commit
groups.kicker: The stamp script asks Git only at a root with its own .git, and logs no phrase for a release
intro: scripts/stamp-build.mjs runs at the end of pnpm build. It asks Git for the commit at the package root, writes the build stamp, and logs one line. It now asks only when the package root holds a .git entry, so an archive unpacked inside another repository stamps {}, as an archive anywhere else does.

The log line drops not a git checkout for a build with no commit. A release install builds twice, once from the prepare step of pnpm install and once from pnpm run build, so the old phrase appeared twice during every install. The stamp's JSON keeps its shape, so its two readers, field --version and the report_build check in install.sh that prints cli-current or cli-stale, read it as before.

files.note: The commit is read only when .git exists at the package root, and the log line names the short commit only when there is one.

checks.text: An archive of this head unpacked under a Git repository with a commit stamped {}. At the previous head, the same setup stamped the outer repository's commit. The review's own worktree, whose .git is a file, still stamped its commit.

Both archive builds logged stamped dist/build-info.json with nothing after it; a checkout build logged stamped dist/build-info.json (af362da). A search of the repository found nothing that parses this line.

files.note: The example's first line becomes field 0.3.0, and the text says a build from a checkout adds its commit.
